title: Somebody Rang The Bell At Four

scenes.narration: Somebody rang the counter bell at four this afternoon. There was nobody at the counter. There were my keys.
scenes.imagePrompt: A brass counter bell on a wooden counter beside a ring of keys tied to a brown luggage tag, the visitor side of the counter empty and dark, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: My keys were clipped to my belt. I had touched them a second before, when I stood up.
scenes.imagePrompt: An empty belt clip on the hip of a person in a grey cardigan standing by a counter, cropped at the waist, no face visible, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: They were already tagged. When I opened the log, they were already in it. Keys, one ring. Handed in, four o'clock.
scenes.imagePrompt: A ring of old keys hanging from a brown luggage tag on string, held up in the light of a single bulb, hands out of frame, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.text: I HAD TO SIGN FOR THEM
scenes.narration: I took them back. I had to sign for them. It is the only line in the log with anything in the claimed by column.
scenes.imagePrompt: A fountain pen resting on an open ledger at the end of a single line of fresh dark ink, the rest of the column blank, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain
